title: Token Parcel Aperture: compact attribution panel + pricing pattern prototype
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Customers need a compact, exportable view that surfaces token-level cost attribution without overwhelming the Console. Current token cost prototypes are either too dense for quick triage or too heavy to export for downstream billing. Goal: ship a lightweight 'Token Parcel Aperture' panel — a collapsed-first UI pattern that reveals a single-line summary per route/flow, with on-demand deep-dive into attribution, pricing bands, and an optimized export flow for large accounts. UX goals: 1) Scannability for engineers and finance leads (compact rows, micro-metrics), 2) Role-aware detail (operators vs. billing admins), 3) Fast export (CSV/NDJSON/Parquet) that respects privacy (PII redaction options) and scale (server-side pagination + sampling), 4) Clear mapping from UI to price model (per-token vs. slab tiers) so users can predict cost impact of config changes. This ticket covers: surface-level mocks, an interactive Figma prototype for compact-to-expanded transitions, acceptance criteria for PM/Eng handoff, and a recommended export contract for backend implementation.
acceptance_criteria: Compact panel shows: route name, total tokens, inferred cost (USD), cost-per-message, 7d sparkline mini-chart, and a chevron to expand
Expanded view surfaces: per-prompt attribution rows, model variant, quantization hint, cache hits, and list of top 3 contributing prompts with truncated preview
Export button exposes format choices (CSV, NDJSON, Parquet), date range picker, role-based column toggle, and PII redaction switch
Export contract defined: server-side pagination, max 100k rows per export job, optional sampling parameter, and async job with callback URL
Design tokens and accessibility: high-contrast colors, keyboard-expandable rows, and aria-labels for screen readers
Prototype validated in 3 usability sessions with engineers and a billing lead; at least 80% of tasks completed without clarification

decisions: Use collapsed-first UX to maximize scan-ability on the default Console route list
Expose 'estimated cost' rather than 'exact cost' to set user expectations about rounding and model assumptions
Server-side export with pagination + sampling to balance precision and performance for large customers
Parquet export is optional: add as an extra workstream behind a feature flag (release-2026.04)
